blocks.x: Fall in New York City is a season worth celebrating!
From golden leaves lining our neighborhood streets to crisp afternoons that practically beg for a long walk, there’s something special about watching the city transform as autumn arrives.

But if you’re craving a little more greenery this season, you don’t have to travel far to find it. Just a short trip across the Hudson River, Branch Brook Park in Newark, New Jersey, offers 360 acres of winding paths, picturesque waterways, historic bridges, and colorful autumn scenery. Best known for its spectacular cherry blossoms in the spring, this sprawling urban oasis deserves a spot on your fall foliage bucket list, too.
Branch Brook Park is a historic oasis just outside NYC

Located in Newark and extending into neighboring Belleville, Branch Brook Park is a 360-acre public park with a fascinating history. It was envisioned by legendary landscape architect Frederick Law Olmsted Sr., whose work also helped shape New York’s Central Park, before the Olmsted Brothers firm developed the park’s landscape plans in the late 19th century.

Today, its expansive lawns, mature trees, streams, and gently rolling terrain make it a lovely place to escape the city’s hustle and bustle. The park is also recognized on both the New Jersey and National Registers of Historic Places, adding another layer of history to a leisurely autumn stroll.

Where to see fall foliage at Branch Brook Park

While Branch Brook Park is famous for its springtime blossoms, autumn brings a different kind of beauty to its expansive landscape. Its mix of wooded areas, open meadows, waterways, and mature trees creates plenty of opportunities to take in the changing season.

For a scenic walk, follow the paths around Branch Brook Lake, where you can enjoy views across the water and toward the park’s surrounding landscape. The park also has winding trails and historic pedestrian bridges that offer picturesque places to pause, snap a few photos, and enjoy a slower afternoon outdoors.

Fall colors change with the weather each year, so the exact timing and intensity of the foliage can vary. If you’re planning a visit specifically for peak color, check recent local foliage updates before heading out.

Take a scenic walk past the lake and historic bridges

One of the park’s biggest draws is its varied scenery. Rather than a single stretch of trees, Branch Brook Park features a combination of open green spaces, meandering streams, ponds, and bridges woven throughout its landscape.

Start near Branch Brook Lake for a relaxing waterfront walk, then explore more of the park’s paved pathways. The park stretches for nearly four miles, so you can make your outing as short or as leisurely as you like.
The park is famous for more than 5,300 cherry blossom trees

Of course, Branch Brook Park’s signature attraction arrives in spring. The park is home to more than 5,300 Japanese flowering cherry trees across 18 varieties, making it one of the country’s most celebrated destinations for cherry blossom viewing.

Each year, the trees draw visitors for the Essex County Cherry Blossom Festival. But once the blossoms have faded, the park remains a beautiful destination for walks, cycling, and enjoying the changing seasons.
In other words, you don’t have to wait until spring to appreciate this Newark gem.

Shutterstock / George Wirt
How to get to Branch Brook Park from NYC

One of the best parts of visiting Branch Brook Park is that you don’t necessarily need a car. The Newark Light Rail runs along the park’s western side, with several stops providing access to different sections of the grounds.

You can connect to the light rail from Newark Penn Station, making a public-transit trip from Manhattan a practical option. If you’re driving, the park has multiple access points throughout Newark and Belleville.
The park is free to visit and open daily from dawn until 10 p.m., making it an easy addition to your fall weekend plans.

So, if you’re looking for a seasonal escape that doesn’t require a long journey, Branch Brook Park is well worth exploring. Whether you’re strolling beside the lake, admiring its historic landscape, or simply enjoying a little fresh air beneath the autumn trees, this 360-acre park offers a lovely reminder that fall beauty can be found just beyond the city limits.
